quick_start_dialog.title: Quick Start
quick_start_dialog.content:
Welcome to EVD. There are many powerful tools here, but you do not need to learn everything at once. You can open your first video and make basic edits within a few minutes.

Many actions will already feel familiar. You can open a file with Ctrl+O; move through the video with the arrow keys, Ctrl+Left / Right, Home, End, and Page Up / Page Down; and use the standard logic for selecting, copying, and deleting. For example, Ctrl+A selects the whole video, Ctrl+Shift+Home / End selects to the beginning or end, and Ctrl+Shift+Left / Right Arrow selects between markers. You do not need to memorize every shortcut. You can discover commands naturally by visiting the relevant menus.

One of EVD's biggest strengths is that AI support is available in almost every stage of your work. You can have the current point described, check inserted text, images, overlays, and verify many results with AI. Just remember to enter your API key first from the AI menu.

Start by opening a video and moving through it. If you like, place markers with M at important points and work around them. Then try selecting a section, listening only to the selection, deleting an unnecessary part, and adding more markers if needed. Silence cleanup, noise cleanup, and volume adjustment tools can save you a great deal of time, especially in spoken recordings.

When you are ready, you can add audio, images, text, overlays, transitions, and subtitles from the Insert menu. Later, you can move on to tools such as the object library, slideshow creation, external audio sync, and video layer support. EVD is here not only for editing, but also for accessible recording and live broadcast preparation.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.content:
Welcome to EVD

EVD is a keyboard-first video editor built so blind and low-vision users can work with video independently. The goal is not only to cut footage, but also to enrich it by adding text, visuals, music, subtitles, and AI-assisted guidance.

This help section is designed to explain not just which button to press, but also what each feature is for, when it is useful, and how to use it step by step.

You can start with the menu bar and playback topics, then move on to text, image, audio, recording wizard, and vertical video topics as needed.

How to open this help: Open Help > User Guide or press F2.

menu_bar.title: Menu Bar Overview
menu_bar.content:
How to Think About the Menu Bar

All major EVD features are organized in the menu bar. Press Alt to move to it, use Left and Right Arrow to move between menus, and Down Arrow to inspect the commands inside a menu.

  • File: Project open/save, export, audio-only export, sync wizards, and language settings.
  • Edit: Cut, copy, paste, delete, selection tools, video properties, audio settings, and silence analysis.
  • Play: Playback, pause, play selection, seeking, and time navigation commands.
  • Insert: Text, audio, image, video layer, subtitle, transition, CTA/overlay, and vertical video tools.
  • View: Rotation and fullscreen options.
  • Go: Quick movement to the start, end, middle, markers, and selection boundaries.
  • Markers: Marker creation and management.
  • AI: Description, smart selection, and API key management.
  • Help: Shortcuts, shortcut manager, and this help system.

When you are unsure where a feature lives, ask yourself whether it is about the file itself, editing, playback, or inserting something new into the video. That mental model makes the menu easier to learn.

Quick access: Press Alt to move to the menu bar at any time.

api_key.title: Enter Gemini API Key
api_key.content:
First-Time Setup for AI Features

Most AI-assisted features in EVD require a Google Gemini API key. If you want to use current-position description, selection description, suitable-area suggestions for visuals, or similar smart tools, this step is necessary.

  1. Open the AI menu.
  2. Select Gemini API Key....
  3. Paste your API key into the field.
  4. Choose Gemini 2.5 Flash for faster responses or Gemini 1.5 Flash for more economical use.
  5. Press Save.

You usually need to do this only once. If AI answers stop appearing later, checking this setting is the first thing to do.

Menu path: AI > Gemini API Key...

location_desc.title: Describe Current Position
location_desc.content:
Learn What Is Happening Around the Current Moment

This feature helps you understand what is happening around the exact point where the video is paused. It is useful when you first explore a video, check whether a scene has changed, or verify whether your insertions were applied at the right place.

  1. Pause the video at the point you want to inspect.
  2. Run AI > Describe Current Position. To do this, open the AI menu and choose Describe Current Position, or press Ctrl+Alt+V.
  3. The AI analyzes a few seconds around that moment and returns a spoken and visible explanation.

It is especially useful after adding a logo, subtitle, or text overlay, because it can help you verify whether the new element overlaps important content.

Open it from: AI > Describe Current Position or press Ctrl+Alt+V.

smart_selection.title: Smart Selection
smart_selection.content:
Check Whether Your Selection Feels Natural

Sometimes a selected range is technically correct but still awkward, for example because it cuts in the middle of a sentence or ends too close to a scene change. Smart Selection helps you review that decision before you commit to an edit.

  1. Select a range.
  2. Run AI > Smart Selection. You can open the AI menu and choose Smart Selection, or press Ctrl+I.
  3. Read the feedback.
  4. If needed, extend or shorten the range and test again.

This is especially useful in speech-heavy videos, interviews, and tutorial content where natural timing matters.

Open it from: AI > Smart Selection or press Ctrl+I.

selection_desc.title: Describe Selection
selection_desc.content:
Understand a Specific Range in Detail

This command focuses on the range you selected instead of the entire video. It is ideal when you want to understand a particular scene before deleting it, speeding it up, or adding something on top of it.

  1. Select a part of the video.
  2. Run AI > Describe Selection. You can open the AI menu and choose Describe Selection, or press Ctrl+Alt+D.
  3. If needed, ask an extra follow-up question.
  4. Use the answer to decide whether to keep, remove, or adjust that segment.

It helps answer practical questions like whether a person is visible, whether the scene contains a product shot, or whether the area is suitable for a text overlay.

Open it from: AI > Describe Selection or press Ctrl+Alt+D.

new_project.title: New Slide or Video Project
new_project.content:
Choosing the Right Starting Point

EVD supports two different ways to begin work. One is for editing an existing video. The other is for building a slideshow-style project from scratch.

  • File > New: Clears the current editing session and starts with a blank workspace.
  • File > New Slide Project: Starts a slideshow workflow using images, audio, text, and narration.

If you already have a video file, opening that file is usually the right choice. If you only have images and audio and want to create a video from them, the slide project is the better starting point.

Menu path: Open File > New for a blank editing session or File > New Slide Project for a slideshow workflow.

save_options.title: Save Options
save_options.content:
Saving a Project Is Not the Same as Exporting a Video

EVD has two separate save concepts, and understanding the difference prevents confusion.

  • Save Project (.kve / .eng): Stores the editing structure so you can come back later and continue working.
  • Save Video As: Creates the final playable video file.
  • Export Audio Only: Exports just the audio track.
  • Save Selection: Exports only the selected part.

A good habit is to save the project first, then export the video. That way you can reopen the work later if you want to change anything.

Menu path: Most save commands are under the File menu.

select_delete.title: Selection and Deletion
select_delete.content:
Build a Reliable Selection Workflow

Many powerful features in EVD depend on a correct selection. Once a range is selected, you can delete it, change its speed, ask AI about it, or play only that area.

  • Shift + Left / Right Arrow: Expands selection in small steps.
  • Ctrl+Shift+Left / Right Arrow: Selects up to the previous or next marker.
  • Select Between Markers: Creates a quick selection between markers.
  • Ctrl+Shift+Home / End: Selects from the start to the cursor or from the cursor to the end.

Delete

After making a selection, press Delete to remove it. If you are not fully sure, play the selection first or ask AI to describe it before deleting.

Useful shortcuts: Shift+Left/Right, Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right, Delete.

playback.title: Playback Controls
playback.content:
Move Through the Timeline with Confidence

Playback controls are important not only for watching, but also for making accurate edits.

  • Space: Plays and pauses, often in a preview-style behavior.
  • Enter: If the video is playing, it stops exactly at the current position and leaves the cursor there. If the video is already paused, it continues from that same point. This still makes Enter one of the safest ways to prepare for a cut.
  • Shift+Space: Plays only the selected area.
  • Left / Right Arrow: Moves in small steps.
  • Ctrl+Left / Right Arrow: Jumps in larger steps.
  • Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End: Moves to the beginning or end.

A practical workflow is: play, stop with Enter, then use selection or markers. If needed, press Enter again to continue from the same spot. That pattern is usually faster and more precise than editing while the video keeps moving.

Useful shortcuts: Space, Enter, Shift+Space, Ctrl+Left/Right, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End.

add_text.title: Adding Text
add_text.content:
Why and When to Add Text

Text is useful for titles, short notes, quotes, warnings, or highlighting an important message. It is especially effective in educational videos, announcements, and social media content.

  1. Open Insert > Add Text.
  2. Type the message you want to show.
  3. Choose font, size, color, background, and shadow settings.
  4. Pick a position, or use Suggest Style and Position for AI guidance.
  5. If needed, use Comment on Current State to ask the AI whether the current styling and placement work well.
  6. Decide whether the text should stay for the whole video or only for a specific duration.

A practical tip is to ask the AI to comment on the current state, then adjust the settings manually. That often gives more controlled results than blindly applying the first suggestion.

Menu path: Insert > Add Text.

add_audio.title: Adding Audio
add_audio.content:
Add Music, Effects, or Extra Voice Layers

The audio insertion tool can be used for background music, voice-over, short sound effects, or recorded narration. It helps you enrich the original soundtrack without permanently losing the original audio.

  1. Open Insert > Add Audio.
  2. Choose Select File to add an audio file or Record to capture new audio.
  3. Adjust the inserted audio level and the original video audio level separately.
  4. Use Preview to listen and refine the balance.
  5. Decide whether the sound should play once or loop as background music.

If speech clarity matters, keep the background music low. Music should support the mood, not overpower the spoken content.

Menu path: Insert > Add Audio.

add_image.title: Adding Image or Logo
add_image.content:
Place a Logo, Watermark, or Visual Overlay

This tool is ideal for adding logos, watermarking a video, placing a graphic on the screen, or using a background visual. It is especially helpful for YouTube, promotional videos, and branded business content.

  1. Open Insert > Add Image.
  2. In the first step, choose the purpose: Watermark/Logo, Free Visual, or Background Visual.
  3. In the second step, choose the image file.
  4. In the third step, instead of dealing with coordinates, you can use Suggest Suitable Areas so the AI finds safer empty spaces on the screen.
  5. You can also use Comment on Current State to check whether the current placement looks balanced and non-intrusive.
  6. In the final step, decide whether the image stays for the whole video or only during a chosen time range.

For logos and watermarks, a small corner placement is usually the safest approach. For larger visuals, AI guidance becomes even more valuable.

Menu path: Insert > Add Image.

recording_wizard.title: Accessible Recording Wizard
recording_wizard.content:
Record Screen, Camera, and Microphone with OBS

The Accessible Recording Wizard gives you a more guided and screen-reader-friendly way to use OBS Studio. It is ideal for lessons, software demonstrations, narrated presentations, and tutorial-style recordings.

  1. Open the wizard and choose the recording mode.
  2. Test the OBS connection. Enter host, port, and password if needed.
  3. Choose whether you want to capture a full screen or a specific window.
  4. Optionally enable a camera overlay and system audio, and make sure the microphone is selected.
  5. Try one of the layout presets. If the camera feels too small or covers important content, ask the AI for a suggestion.
  6. Check audio settings, then start recording in the final step.

This wizard is especially useful when you need a repeatable setup for instructional content. When the recording ends, you can immediately open the recording folder or copy the output path.

Menu path / shortcut: File > Accessible Recording Wizard or Ctrl+Shift+R.

zoom_recording.title: Tips for Recording Zoom
zoom_recording.content:
Capture the Zoom Window More Cleanly

Zoom usually produces a cleaner window capture, but extra participant boxes or empty video areas can still appear if the meeting layout is not simplified before recording.

  1. Keep the Zoom meeting in a separate window.
  2. If possible, use Speaker View or the simplest meeting layout.
  3. If a participant has the camera turned off, an empty or camera-off box may appear in areas such as the bottom right. Simplify the Zoom layout when this happens.
  4. Before recording, make sure chat, participants, and similar side panels are closed.
  5. Take a short test recording and adjust the meeting view if needed.

Tip: If the Zoom window already looks clean, EVD usually does not need an extra fix. The most important part is the Zoom meeting layout itself.

meet_recording.title: Tips for Recording Google Meet
meet_recording.content:
Capture the Google Meet Window More Cleanly

Because Google Meet runs inside a web browser, a recording may show not only the speakers but also parts of the browser and the Meet interface. Preparing the window before recording matters more here.

  1. Open Meet in a separate browser window if possible.
  2. Before the meeting starts, close settings, chat, participants, and similar panels.
  3. Maximize the browser window first, and if possible switch to full screen with F11.
  4. Wait a few seconds without moving the mouse so the bottom control bar can hide.
  5. Do not open extra windows or settings during the recording, because they can appear directly in the capture.

Important: The Meet control bar and some window elements can behave like part of the content itself, so seeing them in a window recording can be normal. The cleanest result comes from simplifying the meeting view before you start.

vertical_video.title: Creating Vertical Video (Shorts/Reels)
vertical_video.content:
Turn Horizontal Video into a Social Media Format

This tool converts an existing video into a 9:16 vertical format suitable for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, or TikTok. It is helpful when you already have a horizontal video and want a social-media-friendly version without recording again.

  1. Open Insert > Create Vertical Video (Shorts/Reels).
  2. Select the source video and the output folder.
  3. Choose a framing strategy such as crop, blurred background, or letterbox.
  4. If needed, ask AI for a framing suggestion based on the visible focus area.
  5. Preview the result and then create the vertical output.

This is especially useful for interviews, tutorials, and product clips that were originally captured in horizontal format. If the subject is not centered, AI suggestions can help preserve the most important visual area.

Menu path: Insert > Create Vertical Video (Shorts/Reels).

selection_list.title: Selection List
selection_list.content:
Collect Several Ranges Before Processing

The selection list lets you collect multiple ranges from a long video, reorder them, and process them later as a group.

  1. Select a range in the video.
  2. Use Insert > Add Selected Range to Selection List.
  3. Clear the selection, choose another range, and keep adding items.
  4. Open Insert > Selection List.
  5. Preview items, remove them, or move them up and down.
  6. When ready, merge the list into one clip or create vertical videos from the selection list.

Menu path: Insert > Selection List.

live_effects_panel.title: Live Effects Panel
live_effects_panel.content:
An Effect Bank for Recording and Streaming

The Live Effects Panel helps you prepare the audio, video, and optional visual effects that you want to trigger quickly during a recording or live stream.

  1. Open Accessible Video Recording > Live Effects Panel.
  2. Select a profile or create a new one.
  3. Add audio or video files to slots. You can also attach an image to audio slots.
  4. Choose intro and outro effect slots if needed.
  5. Enable the live effects layer in the recording wizard and trigger the effects during the session.
  6. Inside the panel you can use Alt+R, Alt+1-0, Alt+P, and Alt+Ctrl+P for faster navigation and preview.

Menu path: Accessible Video Recording > Live Effects Panel.

transitions.title: Adding Transition Effects
transitions.content:
Make Cuts Feel Smoother

Transitions soften the jump between two clips or two scenes. They are not always necessary, but they can make promotional, vlog, or slideshow-style content feel more polished.

  1. Move the cursor to the point where you want the transition.
  2. For a quick option, apply the default transition.
  3. For more control, open the Transition Library.
  4. Choose the duration and, if you want, an extra sound effect.
  5. Review the result by listening or describing the area again.

Not every edit needs a transition. Informational videos often benefit from subtle effects, while promotional content can handle stronger transitions.

Menu path / shortcut: Open Insert > Transition > Transition Library, or use T for the active transition in non-Turkish layouts.

subtitles.title: Adding Subtitles
subtitles.content:
Use Subtitles as Text, Speech, or Both

The subtitle tool can do more than simply burn an SRT file into the video. It can also turn subtitles into spoken audio using TTS, which makes it useful for accessibility and alternative output workflows.

  1. Open Insert > Add Subtitle File.
  2. Select an SRT file.
  3. Choose what you want to do next: embed subtitles into the video, speak them with TTS, or do both.
  4. If you choose TTS, review the voice, speed, and mixing settings.
  5. When the process finishes, open the result and verify it.

This feature is especially useful for accessible media, educational content, and social media videos that may be watched without sound.

Menu path: Insert > Add Subtitle File.

insertion_list.title: Insertion Queue
insertion_list.content:
Apply Several Insertions in One Pass

Instead of rendering each audio, text, or visual addition immediately, you can queue multiple insertions and process them together. This saves time when you are building up a more complex edit.

  1. While adding an item, choose Add to Queue instead of applying it immediately.
  2. Repeat this for the other items you want to add.
  3. Open Insert > Insertion Queue.
  4. Review the list and remove or adjust items if needed.
  5. Apply everything in a single batch.

This is especially convenient when you want to add a logo, some text, and background music to the same video without waiting after every single step.

Menu path: Insert > Insertion Queue.

broadcast_room_overview.title: Broadcast Room Overview
broadcast_room_overview.content:
What Is the Broadcast Room?

The Broadcast Room is an accessible live production workspace for inviting guests, building scene layouts, recording, going live on YouTube, sharing screens, and triggering live effects.

Think of it in two layers. First you establish the room connection. Then you decide how that connection should look on screen and in the recording by choosing a scene layout.

  • Room and devices: Room creation, persistent rooms, camera, microphone, and speaker selection.
  • Participants and chat: Guest list, hand raise, private message, and send-to-all message flows.
  • Sharing and sources: Host screen share, guest screen share, and local source selection.
  • Scene layout: Who is left, who is right, whether the screen is large, and whether faces are small.
  • Recording and streaming: OBS preparation, local recording, YouTube live streaming, and the effects layer.

Menu path: Record > Broadcast Room.

broadcast_room_interface.title: Broadcast Room Interface
broadcast_room_interface.content:
How to Think About the Interface

At the top of the Broadcast Room there is a Region List. Press Alt+L to move there, use the arrow keys to browse regions, and press Enter to jump to the first control of the selected region.

The main regions are:

  • Live Preview: A large preview of the host, guests, and any active screen share.
  • Room and Devices: Room creation, persistent rooms, and device selections.
  • Participants and Chat: Message history, host message composer, and the participant list.
  • Sharing and Sources: Host local sharing and capturable sources.
  • Scene Layout: Side-by-side, large share, or small faces style layouts.
  • OBS, Recording, YouTube, Effects: The sections that actually run the live workflow.
  • Diagnostics and Event History: The place to inspect connection, sharing, audio, and participant events.

Fast navigation: Use Ctrl+Right and Ctrl+Left to move between regions like a ribbon.

broadcast_room_open_room.title: How to Open a Room
broadcast_room_open_room.content:
Open a Temporary Room

  1. Open the Broadcast Room.
  2. Check your camera, microphone, and speaker selections.
  3. If needed, edit the host name and room name.
  4. Press Create Room.
  5. When the room is ready, the invite link is copied to the clipboard so you can share it with a guest.

A temporary room is the fastest path for a rehearsal, a one-time call, or an immediate live session.

What Does the Guest Do?

The guest opens the link, types a display name, optionally enables camera and microphone, and joins with Join Room. If the room rules require a password, the password field appears automatically.

broadcast_room_persistent_rooms.title: Persistent Rooms and Rules
broadcast_room_persistent_rooms.content:
Why Use a Persistent Room?

If you want to reuse the same link again and again, a persistent room is more practical. You do not need to send a new invite link every time.

  1. Open Room Management.
  2. Set the room name, host name, and optionally the persistent room key.
  3. If you want password protection, enter a room password.
  4. Choose whether a password should be required when the host is present or absent.
  5. Choose whether guests may enter while the host is not connected.
  6. Press Create Room with These Settings.

After creation, the room appears in the Persistent Room List. You can move through that list with Up and Down Arrow, press Enter to open the selected room, and press Right Arrow to open its context menu.

The persistent room menu includes copy link, change password rules, enable or disable host-absent access, and edit room options.

broadcast_room_layouts.title: Scene Layouts
broadcast_room_layouts.content:
What Is a Scene Layout?

A scene layout decides how the host and guests appear in the recording or live stream. Joining the room is not the same as being placed in the scene. People join first, then you choose how the scene should present them.

Common examples include:

  • Two speakers side by side: Useful for interviews and balanced conversations.
  • Large share, small faces: Best for presentations, teaching, and screen explanations.
  • Large faces, small share: Good when the share supports the conversation but the speakers remain the main focus.
  • Single-speaker focus: Best for one-person live sessions.

When a guest starts screen sharing, the system can offer quick scene suggestions, but it does not force a layout change. The host remains in control.

Tip: After choosing a layout, use Ask AI for Feedback to verify whether faces and the share are actually framed well.

broadcast_room_recording.title: How to Record
broadcast_room_recording.content:
Local Recording Flow

  1. Make sure the OBS connection and required sources are ready.
  2. If guests are connected, choose your scene layout.
  3. Prepare any needed sharing or effects.
  4. Press Start Recording or use Alt+R.
  5. During recording you can still change the scene layout, manage participants, and start sharing if needed.
  6. When finished, stop the recording with the same control.

The newer architecture uses a dedicated Broadcast Output idea so the host controls do not appear in the recording while you continue managing the session.

Tip: Whenever you are trying a new layout or effect setup, record a short rehearsal first.

broadcast_room_youtube.title: YouTube Live Workflow
broadcast_room_youtube.content:
Before You Go Live on YouTube

The YouTube path is similar to local recording, but it also includes account, broadcast plan, and stream key steps.

  1. Finish your OBS and Broadcast Room setup.
  2. Verify the connected YouTube account.
  3. If you are creating a new live stream, review the title, description, and visibility options.
  4. If needed, select an existing scheduled broadcast.
  5. Press Start Live Stream.
  6. Once live, you can continue managing participants, screen sharing, and effects.

Tip: A private or unlisted YouTube test stream is a very good final check before a real broadcast.

broadcast_room_effects.title: Effects Layer
broadcast_room_effects.content:
When Should You Use the Effects Layer?

The effects layer is for jingles, transition videos, short audio stingers, and visual effect cues. It is especially useful for openings, mid-show transitions, and closing moments.

  1. Create an effects profile in advance or choose an existing one.
  2. Assign audio, video, and optional visuals to slots.
  3. Enable that profile inside the Broadcast Room.
  4. Trigger the correct slot at the right moment during the session.

Anything played through the effects layer goes into the recording and the live output. Keeping opening, middle, and closing effects in separate slots makes the workflow easier.

broadcast_room_screen_share.title: Screen Sharing
broadcast_room_screen_share.content:
Host and Guest Sharing

Both the host and guests can share their screen, but the host decides when sharing is allowed and how it is presented.

Host Sharing

  1. Press Alt+S to open the sharing area.
  2. Choose the entire screen, a window, or another suitable local source.
  3. If needed, include system audio.
  4. After the share begins, place it as a large or small element in the chosen scene layout.

Guest Sharing

When a guest starts sharing, the browser's own screen-share dialog opens. The guest chooses a window, tab, or full screen there. If the browser and operating system support it, share audio can also be included through that same browser dialog.

Once sharing starts, the host receives an announcement and quick scene suggestions become available.

broadcast_room_participants.title: Participant Management and Chat
broadcast_room_participants.content:
Participant List

Press Alt+U to move to the participant list. Move with Up and Down Arrow. Press Right Arrow to open the selected participant's menu and Left Arrow to close it.

The participant menu includes:

  • Remove from room
  • Send private message
  • Turn audio on or off
  • Turn video on or off
  • Enable or disable camera, microphone, and screen-share permissions
  • Mark a hand raise as seen

Chat and Hand Raise

Press Alt+C to move to chat. The host can send a message to everyone and can also send a private message from the participant menu. Guests have both send-to-all and send-to-host flows.

Guests can use Raise Hand to request the floor. The host hears that request and also sees it in the hand-raise area.

broadcast_room_shortcuts.title: Essential Shortcuts
broadcast_room_shortcuts.content:
Host Shortcuts

  • Alt+A: Toggle host microphone.
  • Alt+V: Toggle host video.
  • Alt+S: Open sharing, or stop sharing if it is already active.
  • Alt+Y: Move to layout selection.
  • Alt+U: Move to the participant list or reveal it.
  • Alt+C: Move to the chat panel.
  • Alt+O: Open or close Room Management.
  • Alt+Q: Close the room.
  • Alt+R: Start or stop recording.
  • Alt+L: Move to the Region List.
  • Alt+Ctrl+L: Start or stop YouTube Live while the Broadcast Room is open.
  • Alt+Ctrl+Y: Read the current YouTube broadcast statistics.

Guest Web Shortcuts

  • Ctrl+D: Toggle microphone.
  • Ctrl+E: Toggle video.
  • Ctrl+Shift+E: Start or stop screen sharing.
  • Ctrl+Shift+H: Leave the room.

Tip: Many controls announce their shortcut when focused, so users can learn the workflow naturally while operating the interface.

broadcast_room_ai_review.title: Ask AI for Feedback
broadcast_room_ai_review.content:
What Does the AI Review Do?

The Ask AI for Feedback button in the live preview captures the current real frame and returns an accessibility-oriented evaluation.

It focuses on questions like:

  • Are the host and selected guest faces actually visible?
  • If screen sharing is active, does the share fit the chosen layout together with the faces?
  • Are faces too small, cropped, or misplaced?
  • Is there an unwanted control, black gap, or other distracting visual element on screen?

This feature is especially valuable as a last pre-broadcast check for blind users. Choose the layout, start sharing if needed, then ask AI for feedback.

broadcast_room_troubleshooting.title: Broadcast Room Troubleshooting
broadcast_room_troubleshooting.content:
Most Common Situations

  • A guest joined but there is no audio: Check camera and microphone permissions, browser site permissions, and selected devices.
  • No shared image appears: Check whether the guest truly started sharing and whether the share track appears in diagnostics.
  • No share audio: Check whether the browser actually offers audio for the chosen share source. Some browsers only provide share audio for specific share types.
  • Controls appear in the recording: Verify that the clean scene and broadcast output flow are active, then take a short test recording.
  • The participant list or chat behaves strangely: Reopen the app and do a quick rehearsal before the real session.

The Diagnostics and Event History area is the first place to inspect share audio, video tracks, and participant events.

OBS WebSocket Setup Steps:
  1. Open OBS Studio.
  2. Go to the Tools menu and open the WebSocket Server Settings.
  3. Enable the WebSocket server.
  4. Note the port and password if you set one, then click Apply.
  5. Match those values here and run the connection test.
